question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Equation of a Tangent Line to a Curve at a Point
question.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}-x$ at the point $(1,3).$
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}-x.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =-12{x}^{-4}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(1)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1)=-12(1)^{-4}-1=-13.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=-13$ and the coordinates of our point $(1,3),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(3) & =-13(x-1) \\ y & =-13x+13+3 \\ y & =-13x+16.\end{aligned}
$$
